text:
I need help with the narrative section of a grant application. I'm the director of a volunteer-run food bank in a town of about 9,000 people, and we're applying to our county community foundation for a refrigerated van.

What I have:
- We hand out about 38,000 pounds of food a month to 610 households. About 6,000 pounds of that is fresh produce, milk and eggs.
- Last summer, local farms offered us roughly 9,000 pounds of produce over three months that we had to turn down because we had no way to pick it up cold or store it.
- The van costs $68,000. We're asking the foundation for $50,000 and covering the other $18,000 from our reserves, which would leave us with $11,000.
- We have 23 regular volunteers. Four of them have said they would drive the van on a weekly schedule.
- The foundation gave us $12,000 for shelving in 2023. Our final report on that grant was four months late.

I want the narrative to say the van will let us double the amount of fresh food we hand out in the first year. The narrative is limited to 500 words.

Before I write the narrative, there are a few things to settle, because one of them changes the main claim.

**The argument as I see it**

- **Claim:** A $50,000 grant toward a refrigerated van will let the food bank give out a lot more fresh food, starting in the first year.
- **Grounds:** You give out 38,000 lb a month to 610 households, and 6,000 lb of that is fresh. Last summer you turned down 9,000 lb of farm produce because you couldn't keep it cold. You're paying $18,000 of the cost yourselves. Four volunteers have agreed to drive weekly.
- **Warrant:** If you can transport and keep cold food, you can accept more of it. More fresh food on hand means more fresh food going out to households.
- **Backing:** You've already been offered the food, and you have drivers ready. The foundation has funded you before.
- **Rebuttals the committee will raise:** whether the claim is realistic, who pays to run the van, whether the drivers will keep showing up, and the late report on the 2023 grant. The committee knows about that report, so the narrative should deal with it before making the ask.

**The "double in the first year" claim**

Your current figures don't support it yet. Doubling means about 72,000 more pounds of fresh food a year, or 6,000 more a month. The food you can point to is the 9,000 lb from farms. Over a year that's about a 12% increase. During the three summer months it's 50%, going from 6,000 to 9,000 lb a month.

A version your figures support: *"In harvest months, the van will let us take in the 3,000 lb a month of local produce we had to turn down last summer, which raises the fresh food we give out by half."* We could add a checkpoint, such as reporting the pounds taken in by a set date.

A committee member who does the arithmetic will see that 9,000 lb doesn't double 72,000 lb. If they see it themselves, they may start doubting your other numbers too. Doubling could still be true if the van opens up other sources. That's my first question below.

**Questions (most important first)**

1. **Other fresh food the van would open up.** Would it let you take food from grocery stores, a regional food bank, dairies or egg farms that you can't take now? Any pounds or offers you can name would help. This decides whether the doubling claim stays in.
2. **The late 2023 report.** Why was it four months late, and what have you changed since then? For example, a named person who owns reporting, or a calendar. The committee will remember it, and one sentence on the fix will help more than leaving it out.
3. **Running costs.** Do you know the yearly cost of insurance, fuel and maintenance, and how you'll pay it? This matters more because your reserves would drop to $11,000.
4. **Cold storage at the food bank.** Do you have enough refrigerator or cooler space to hold the extra food once the van brings it in? Last summer you also turned food down for lack of storage.
5. **Drivers.** Do the four drivers need a particular license, and do you have someone to fill in when a driver can't come?
6. **Anything else the committee knows or will find out.** Is there a cost, a limit or a past problem you haven't mentioned, like a vehicle quote that expires or a deadline on the farm offers?

Once you've answered, I'll write the narrative within 500 words. If you don't know an answer, I'll leave that point out rather than guess.

1. I don't know of any other sources the van would open up. You're right about the math, so drop the doubling claim and go with what the numbers support.

2. Our treasurer at the time was in the hospital for most of that period. Our treasurer now is Dave Lin. I can name him as responsible for the final report, due 30 days after the grant year ends. I can also send the foundation our fresh food pounds every quarter.

3. Insurance and fuel will be about $4,500 a year. That isn't in our budget yet.

4. I don't know.

5. I don't know.

6. Two of the farms have written letters saying they'll give again if we can pick up cold. But I can't promise the farms will offer the same 9,000 pounds again. The application is due April 1.

I've written the narrative with the claim your numbers support. The van lets you accept the produce you had to turn down: half again as much fresh food in harvest months, and about one-eighth more over the year. It comes to about 400 words.

<final_document>
**Project Narrative: A Refrigerated Van for Fresh Food**

Last summer, local farms offered us about 9,000 pounds of fresh produce over three months. We had to turn all of it down because we had no way to pick it up cold or store it.

Every month our volunteers give out about 38,000 pounds of food to 610 households in a town of about 9,000 people. About 6,000 pounds of that is fresh produce, milk and eggs. In each of those three summer months, the produce we turned away would have raised our fresh food by half.

**What the van will do**

With a refrigerated van, we can collect produce from the farms and keep it cold on the way back to us. In harvest months, accepting the produce we turned down last summer would take our fresh food from about 6,000 pounds a month to about 9,000. Over a full year, that adds about 9,000 pounds of fresh food, roughly one-eighth more than we give out now.

Two of the farms have written to say they will give again if we can pick up cold. We can't promise the farms will offer the same 9,000 pounds every year, so we will report to you what actually comes in.

We are run entirely by volunteers. Of our 23 regular volunteers, four have committed to driving the van on a weekly schedule.

**Accountability**

In 2023 the Foundation gave us $12,000 for shelving. Our final report on that grant was four months late, because our treasurer at the time was in the hospital for most of that period.

Our current treasurer, Dave Lin, will be responsible for the final report on this grant, due 30 days after the grant year ends. We will also send the Foundation our fresh food pounds every quarter. You will see what the van is bringing in throughout the year, not only at the end.

**The request**

The van costs $68,000. We are asking the Foundation for $50,000 and will pay the other $18,000 from our reserves, which is more than a quarter of the cost. That leaves us $11,000 in reserve. Insurance and fuel will cost about $4,500 a year, and that cost is not yet in our budget.

**If we do not get the van**

Without a refrigerated vehicle, we'll be in the same position the next time farms offer us fresh food: our volunteers will have to say no. Last summer that meant 9,000 pounds.
</final_document>

Three things to look at before April 1:

- **The $4,500 a year for insurance and fuel.** The narrative says plainly that it isn't in your budget yet, because I didn't want to make up a plan for paying it. The committee will almost certainly ask about it, especially with reserves dropping to $11,000. If you can name where the money will come from, even "we will add it to the 2027 budget," that one sentence will help a lot.
- **Storage.** Last summer you couldn't store the produce either, not just transport it. If a reviewer asks where the extra 3,000 lb a month will be kept cold, you'll need an answer. If you have enough refrigerator or cooler space, add a sentence saying so.
- **The farm letters.** If the application allows attachments, include the two letters and mention them in the narrative.
